ui.home.giftH: Before any of this is a shop.
ui.home.gift1: You didn’t come here for nothing.
ui.home.gift2: Maybe a link. Maybe a search at an hour you wouldn’t admit to. Either way, something moved you enough to open a page about feelings — and most people scroll straight past those.
ui.home.gift3a: Whatever today has been, you carried it. Nobody watched you do that. There was no moment where someone stopped and said:
ui.home.gift3em: that was heavy, and you did it anyway.
ui.home.gift3b: So let this be that moment. It’s small, and it’s from a stranger, but it counts.
ui.home.gift4: You’re allowed to put it down for a minute. Not solve it. Not be positive about it. Just set it on the floor beside you and sit here, where nothing is being asked of you.
ui.home.gift5: That was free, and there’s no catch attached to it — no email, nothing to close, nothing that follows you.
ui.home.sendH: Sometimes words are easier to send than to say.

ui.home.step1P: The one you’re actually in, or the one you want to be in. Read its opening free first.
ui.home.step2P: One tap on Buy Me a Coffee — card or Apple Pay, a few seconds. Nothing to create, nothing to remember.
ui.home.step3P: Their redirect drops you straight onto your page. Bookmark it — the link stays live for you.
ui.home.who1: Moodshop is one person, not a company.
ui.home.who2: I chose these eight feelings, and I wrote them with AI in the loop — I’m telling you because you’d guess anyway, and I’d rather you hear it from me. What I did was decide what stays: nothing is on this shelf that I wouldn’t send to a friend having a bad night.
ui.home.who3: A dollar or two, on purpose. No account, no email list, nothing follows you after you close the tab.
ui.about.h1: We make tiny pieces of writing for moments that are difficult to put into words.
ui.about.intro1a: Most of what’s written about feelings is written
ui.about.intro1b: feelings. It explains them, ranks them, gives you five steps. By the time you’ve read it you’ve thought about the feeling and you haven’t felt a thing.
ui.about.intro2: Moodshop goes the other way. Each piece here has one job: put one specific feeling in you, then get out of the way.
ui.about.whyP: Because there are nights that don’t have a name yet, and nothing on the internet is built for them. A search engine will give you advice. A friend might be asleep. This is the thing in between — two minutes of writing that meets the exact shape of what you’re in.
ui.about.productP: You’re not buying words; you can get words anywhere. You’re buying a specific two minutes. That’s why the shelf is organised by feeling instead of by title, and why every piece is named after the thing it does to you.
ui.about.shortP: Because a piece that takes two minutes and actually moves you beats one that takes twenty and doesn’t. Around two hundred words each, written to be read slowly, once. Nothing here is trying to be a book.
ui.about.accountsH: Why there are no accounts and no subscription
ui.about.accountsP: Nothing you do here needs to be remembered. You pay once, the page opens, the link stays live, and that’s the end of the relationship unless you want more. There’s no inbox to land in, no card on file, no streak to keep. Moodshop can’t email you — it doesn’t have your address and never asks.
ui.about.expectP: Eight feelings today, more being written. Every one shows you its real first lines before you pay anything, and three full pieces are free. If you buy one and it does nothing for you, say so and I’ll send you a different one.
ui.about.note1: Moodshop is one person, not a company.
ui.about.note2: I chose these eight feelings, and I wrote them with AI in the loop — I’m telling you because you’d guess anyway, and I’d rather you hear it from me. What I did was decide what stays: nothing is on this shelf that I wouldn’t send to a friend having a bad night.
ui.about.terms1: You’re paying for access to one web page (or, for a collection, a set of them). It’s for you — read it as often as you like, bookmark it, send someone the link with a note. Don’t republish it as your own. The writing stays mine; the moment is yours.
ui.about.terms2: Payments are handled entirely by Buy Me a Coffee. Their terms cover the transaction itself. Moodshop never touches your card details.
ui.about.refundsPa: If a piece did nothing for you, message me through Buy Me a Coffee and I’ll refund it or send you a different feeling — your choice. On a ${min}–${max} piece of writing I’d rather fix it than argue about it. If you paid and nothing opened,
ui.about.privacy1: No account, no email list, no card details, no profile. Two privacy-light analytics tools count page views and anonymous events (which feeling was opened, whether a share button was tapped) so I know which pieces people need — never who you are.
ui.about.privacy2: When you send someone a feeling, your note is encoded into the link itself and never reaches a server. There is no database here to hold it.

ui.send.privacy: Nothing you type here is sent anywhere. Your note is encoded into the link itself — no server sees it, and there is no database here to keep it in.

ui.for.aboutHintA: This is Moodshop — tiny pieces of writing for very specific feelings. Whoever sent you this didn’t give away your name or theirs to anybody: the note travelled inside the link and never touched a server.
ui.help.h1: Let’s get you to the feeling.
ui.help.lede: Payments run on Buy Me a Coffee, which means three things can go sideways. Here’s each one, and what actually fixes it.
ui.help.q1: You changed your mind and cancelled
ui.help.a1: Nothing was charged, and nothing is waiting on you. The free opening of every feeling stays where it was, and three full pieces are free to read.
ui.help.q2: The payment was declined or failed
ui.help.a2: Buy Me a Coffee handles cards, Apple Pay and PayPal — if one is refused, another usually isn’t. Nothing reaches Moodshop either way; no half-charge is sitting anywhere. Go back to the feeling and try once more.
ui.help.q3: You paid, and no page opened
ui.help.a3: That’s the one real failure, and it’s on my side: it happens when a piece’s redirect isn’t set up properly. Message me through Buy Me a Coffee — the same place your receipt came from — and say which feeling you bought. I’ll send you the link straight away, and refund it if you’d rather.
ui.help.a3Link: Message me on Buy Me a Coffee →
ui.help.a4: The page you unlocked stays live — it just isn’t listed anywhere and there’s no account to log into, so the bookmark is the only way back. If you’ve lost it, message me with your receipt and I’ll send it again.
ui.help.q5: It didn’t do anything for you
ui.help.a5: Then say so. Refunds on a few dollars of writing aren’t worth anyone’s afternoon, so I’d rather send you a different feeling — but if you want the money back, ask and it’s yours.
ui.e404.h1: Looks like this feeling got lost.
ui.e404.lede: The page you were after isn’t here — moved, mistyped, or never existed. The eight that do exist are just below.

faq.q: What exactly am I paying for?
faq.a: One web page with one short piece of writing on it — around 200 words, set in its own colour and typography for that one feeling. It opens in your browser the second you pay. There's no file, no app, no account.
On purpose. These are meant to be read slowly, once, and felt — not skimmed and filed away. A piece that takes two minutes and actually moves you beats one that takes twenty and doesn't.

faq.q: Can I read something before I pay?
faq.a: Yes — every one of the eight. Each mood page opens with the real first lines of that piece, not a teaser written to sell it. Three other pieces are free in full.

faq.q: Can I send one to someone else?
faq.a: Yes, and it's the best thing here. You can send a feeling to someone before you've bought anything — pick the mood, write a line, and the link carries your note. Nothing is stored anywhere; the note lives in the link itself.
No. Payment happens on Buy Me a Coffee and their redirect takes you straight to the piece. Moodshop stores nothing about you and can't email you even if it wanted to.

faq.q: Can I come back to it later?
faq.a: Yes. The link stays live — bookmark it after you pay and reopen it whenever the feeling comes back around.

faq.q: What if it doesn't do anything for me?
faq.a: Then it cost you a dollar or two and you should tell me so. Message me through Buy Me a Coffee — refunds on a $2 piece of writing aren't worth anyone's afternoon, so I'd rather just send you a different one.

calm.name: Calm
calm.tagline: For when everything feels too loud.
calm.description: A short piece written to slow you down — no breathing app, no advice, just two minutes where nothing is being asked of you.
calm.whatThisIs: Seven short paragraphs that move at the speed you wish today had. It doesn't tell you to relax. It just stops asking.
calm.teaserTitle: Nothing is asking anything of you right now
calm.teaser: Let your eyes rest on this, not read it exactly, just move across it slowly. Breathe in for four. Hold for four. Out for six. You don't need to count out loud — just let the rhythm happen underneath everything else you're thinking about.
calm.teaserTail: Your shoulders have been climbing toward your ears for longer than you realized. Let them drop.
calm.shareLine: Nothing is asking anything of you right now.
calm.seoTitle: Something to read when everything feels too loud
calm.seoKeywords: something calming to read, short writing to slow down, two minute read to calm down

nostalgia.name: Nostalgia
nostalgia.tagline: For when you miss a version of your life that doesn't exist anymore.
nostalgia.description: A short piece about the light in a room you can't go back to, and the person you were standing in it.
nostalgia.whatThisIs: A walk back through the small, specific details memory keeps — the ones that aren't about a place at all.
nostalgia.teaser: The particular gold of late afternoon light through a car window on a drive home from somewhere ordinary. The specific quiet of a house on a Sunday morning before anyone else was awake. A voice calling your name from another room, the exact pitch of it, gone now, but not really —
nostalgia.teaserTail: still filed somewhere in you, ready to surface. There's a version of you that existed in that light.
nostalgia.shareLine: You don't miss the place. You miss who you were there.
nostalgia.seoTitle: Something to read when you miss how things used to be
nostalgia.seoKeywords: nostalgic writing, something to read when you miss the past, short nostalgic story

happiness.name: Happiness
happiness.tagline: For when you forgot you're allowed to feel good.
happiness.description: A short piece that hands back the lightness you've been treating as something you have to earn.
happiness.whatThisIs: Two minutes of permission. Not a pep talk — nobody here is going to tell you to be grateful.
happiness.teaserTitle: The lightness you forgot you had
happiness.teaser: Notice this: right now, nothing is required of you. Not one thing. Let your shoulders find out how far down they can actually go. You are allowed to feel good for no reason — you don't need a permission slip, an achievement, a reason the size of your worry.
happiness.teaserTail: Happiness doesn't have to be earned back like a debt. Sometimes it just arrives.
happiness.shareLine: Happiness doesn't have to be earned back like a debt.
happiness.seoTitle: Something short to read when you want to feel lighter
happiness.seoKeywords: short uplifting writing, something to read to feel better, short inspirational writing

hope.name: Hope
hope.description: A short piece for the part of the night that hasn't broken yet, written without a single promise it can't keep.
hope.whatThisIs: About how change starts before there's any proof of it. No timeline, no guarantee, no forced optimism.
hope.teaserTitle: It's still dark, and the sky is already changing
hope.teaser: You can't see it yet, not really — the light hasn't reached the part of the sky you're looking at. But somewhere past the horizon, it's already begun. That's how mornings work. The change starts before there's any proof of it.
hope.teaserTail: You've been asking things to be different for a while now, and nothing you can point to has shifted.
hope.shareLine: The change starts before there's any proof of it.
hope.seoTitle: Something to read when tomorrow feels uncertain
hope.seoKeywords: something hopeful to read, short writing about hope, words for a hard week

hurt.name: Hurt
hurt.description: A short piece about what someone's choice revealed, and why that's the part that keeps stinging.
hurt.whatThisIs: It doesn't take their side and it doesn't tell you to let it go. It just names the thing accurately.
hurt.teaserTitle: You have every right to feel this
hurt.teaser: Someone you trusted did something that trust wasn't built for. Maybe they said it plainly. Maybe they just showed you, through what they chose over you, exactly how much room you took up in their decisions. Not much, it turns out. Not enough.
hurt.teaserTail: That's the part that stings worst — not the moment itself, but what it revealed.
hurt.shareLine: Not the moment itself. What it revealed.
hurt.seoTitle: Something to read when someone hurt you
hurt.seoKeywords: short writing about being hurt, something to read after being let down, short stories about heartbreak

sorrow.name: Sorrow
sorrow.tagline: For the days that feel heavier than usual.
sorrow.description: A letter that sits down next to you instead of trying to move you along.
sorrow.whatThisIs: Written as a letter. It does not say it gets better, because you've heard that and it didn't help.
sorrow.teaser: I'm not going to tell you it gets better. Not yet. Right now I just want to sit here with you, in the part where it's heavy, and not rush you toward the door marked “fine.”
sorrow.teaserTail: Some things don't resolve. They just get carried differently over time.
sorrow.shareLine: Some things don't resolve. They just get carried differently.
sorrow.seoTitle: Something to read when you're sad and don't want advice
sorrow.seoKeywords: things to read when you're sad, short sad writing, something to read on a heavy day

grief.name: Grief
grief.tagline: For someone or something you still carry with you.
grief.description: A letter written to the shape a person left behind, and to the habits that haven't caught up yet.
grief.whatThisIs: For the ordinary ambushes — a stranger's laugh, a coat like theirs. It calls that love, not failure to move on.
grief.teaserTitle: To the shape they left behind,
grief.teaser: I know you still set the table for one more sometimes, out of habit, before you remember. I know their voice still catches you off guard in ordinary places — a stranger's laugh, a song on the radio, a coat like the one they used to wear.
grief.teaserTail: That's not you being unable to move on. That's just what love does when it loses its address.
grief.shareLine: That's just what love does when it loses its address.
grief.seoTitle: Something to read when you're grieving someone
grief.seoKeywords: something to read when grieving, short writing about grief, words for someone you lost

rage.name: Rage
rage.tagline: For the feeling you don't know where to put.
rage.description: A short piece that agrees with you. No breathing exercise, no both-sides, no calming down.
rage.whatThisIs: Permission to be furious at the correct size. It is the loudest thing on the shelf and it is not sorry.
rage.teaser: You've been so reasonable for so long. Explaining calmly. Giving the benefit of the doubt one more time than it was owed. Swallowing the sharp thing you wanted to say because it wasn't “the right moment.” There's never a right moment for people like that.
rage.teaserTail: You are not too much for being furious about this. You are correctly sized.
rage.shareLine: You are not too much for being furious about this. You are correctly sized.
rage.seoTitle: Something to read when you're angry and tired of being reasonable
rage.seoKeywords: something to read when you're angry, short writing about anger, where to put anger
